**Analysis of the test image:**

- **Affected part:** Single leaf (upper surface visible)
- **Color pattern:** The leaf is predominantly green with pale greenish-yellow spots/patches scattered across the upper surface
- **Spot characteristics:** The pale yellow-green areas lack definite, sharp margins — they are diffuse and blend into surrounding tissue
- **Texture:** Leaf surface appears slightly textured; no obvious white powdery coating
- **No concentric rings** (rules out Early Blight, Target Spot)
- **No water-soaked dark lesions** (rules out Bacterial Spot, Late Blight)
- **No white powder** (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- **No mosaic/mottling pattern** (rules out viral diseases)

**Reasoning:**

The key features — pale greenish-yellow spots with no definite margins on the upper leaf surface, while the leaf remains attached and mostly green — align precisely with **Leaf Mold**. The symptom description states: *"Pale greenish-yellow spots, usually less than 1/4 inch with no definite margins, form on the upper sides of leaves."* The corresponding olive-green velvety sporulation would appear on the underside (not visible in this view). The absence of other diagnostic features (concentric rings, water soaking, powdery coating, vascular symptoms) further supports Leaf Mold over other candidates.
